svg.data-oem-alias: DriveNets NCP-40C8CD (Network Cloud Packet forwarder, 4x1/10 + 40x100 + 8x400). NOT A UFISPACE CLAIM - no UfiSpace document mentions DriveNets. The mapping is internal analysis matching DriveNets' NCP-40C8CD (Q2C+ 7.2T) to this chassis on published silicon and port configuration. Recorded so a search for either name finds this box; no DriveNets figure or artwork is transcribed anywhere in this file.
svg.data-tcam: TCAM option available to meet diverse deployment requirements (datasheet)
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO, ITU-T SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 with an additional licence), T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC, Class C timing accuracy; NOS integration is required to activate any of it
svg.data-gnss: integrated receiver covering GPS/QZSS L1 C/A, GLONASS L1OF, BeiDou B1, SBAS L1 C/A (WAAS, EGNOS, MSAS, GAGAN) and Galileo E1B/C, RF sensitivity -166 dBm; passive and active antennas are both supported and auto-detected (HIG Installing an Antenna)
svg.data-antenna: an active GNSS antenna needs 50 ohm impedance matching, 5 V DC, a noise figure of 1.5 dB maximum and an internal LNA gain of 35-42 dB; the port supplies up to 5 V DC / 150 mA and a surge protector is required (HIG Installing an Antenna)
svg.data-macsec: MACsec on all ports (datasheet feature list)
svg.data-srv6: full Segment Routing over IPv6 (datasheet feature list)
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 25G SFP28 SR/LR; 10G SFP+ SR/LR, up to 40 km
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: the four SFP+ management ports take 10G SFP+ SR/LR from the datasheet's Compatible Transceivers list; no separate reach or media list is published for this block - the HIG's Port Overview table does not cover it at all (see the sfp-plus-management-role gap)
svg.data-sfp28-sharing: the four SFP28/SFP-DD ports are in-band port share with 100GE port 0 (datasheet)
svg.data-timing-cable: 50 ohm SMA coaxial with a 1/4-36UNS-2B connector for GNSS, 50 ohm SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz, shielded RJ45 for ToD and shielded RJ48 for BITS, none longer than 3 m (datasheet Compatible Timing Cable Types; HIG section 12)
svg.data-timing-interfaces: GNSS in on SMA, 10MHz in/out on SMB, 1PPS in/out on SMB, ToD in/out on RJ45, BITS in/out on RJ48
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console
svg.data-sfp-plus-management: 4x 10G SFP+ management ports, numbered 0-3 in their own space
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A; NEBS GR-1089

Datasheet input -40 to -72 V at 60 A; the HIG's DC section gives the maximum system consumption as 1220 W under 400G optics MSA standards and 1524 W with OpenZR+, against the AC build's 1212 W and 1510 W.","kind":"orderable"}},"datasheet":{"title":"UfiSpace S9610-48DX 7.2T 100G/400G Open Aggregation Router Datasheet","url":"https://www.ufispace.com/products/telco/aggregation/s9610-48dx-100g-400g-open-aggregation-router"},"description":"UfiSpace S9610-48DX 100G/400G open disaggregated aggregation router - 2RU white box on Broadcom Qumran2c+ BCM88840 at 7.2 Tbps with an 8 GB deep buffer, 40x QSFP28 40/100G in four blocks of five two-high columns, 8x QSFP-DD 100/400G with 400ZR/OpenZR+ in two 2x2 assemblies in the middle, 4x SFP28/SFP-DD 1/10/25G that share in-band with 100GE port 0, and a separate quad of 10G SFP+ management ports; a full timing block (GNSS on SMA, 10MHz and 1PPS on SMB, ToD on RJ45 and BITS on RJ48) with a Stratum 3E OCXO and Class C 1588v2, MACsec on all ports and SRv6; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 2000 W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, exhaust airflow","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"HIG section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Every traffic port here carries exactly one lamp - forty in the QSFP28 bands, eight in the QSFP-DD blue strips, four on the yellow band - and nothing states what any of them means. The lamp-to-port pairing written here is read off the printed numerals that flank each pair, which is better evidence than a bare count, but it is still an inference. Every lamp keeps the component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["qsfp28","qsfpdd-400g","sfp28","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with known ports up, down and passing traffic","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"Every cage block on this panel is a two-high belly-to-belly assembly, and which row is mirrored is NOT resolved by either front image. At 10x a QSFP column shows a bright perforated EMI strip between its two openings and no asymmetry either side of it; the HIG figure draws the same symmetric pair. The rotation used here - upper port rotate 180, lower unrotated - is ufispace/s9600-56dx's reading of the same cage family carried over, and that file itself records that the S9311-64D's is the other way round, so this is a convention borrowed from one sibling that another sibling contradicts.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["qsfp28","qsfpdd-400g","sfp28","sfp-plus-mgmt"],"wanted":"a straight-on macro photograph of one empty cage column, or a cage part number","what":"cage-lip-orientation"},{"note":"The yellow band above the SFP28/SFP-DD quad prints an up arrow, a numeral, two lamps, a numeral and a down arrow per column, exactly as the green QSFP28 bands do - but at the render's 3.5 px/mm those two numerals are about 1.4 mm of ink and do not resolve at any zoom. The IDs 48-51 are certain, from the HIG's Port Overview table and Figure 8's callout, and are used for every id and rel-pos; what the metal prints beside these four cages is not established, so the arrows and lamps are drawn and the numerals are not. Note that the neighbouring blocks print two different schemes - global 0-39 for QSFP28, local 0-7 for QSFP-DD - so neither can be assumed here.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["sfp28","port-48","port-49","port-50","port-51"],"wanted":"a straight-on high-resolution photograph of the left half of the faceplate","what":"sfp28-band-numerals"},{"note":"The HIG's Component Physical Information table weighs the chassis without FRUs twice, 'Standard: 49.91lb (22.64kg)' and 'Premium: 47.48 lb (21.54kg)', and weighs the total package contents twice the same way, and no other sentence in either document uses either word. The datasheet's only nearby line is 'TCAM option available to meet diverse deployment requirements', which is a plausible but unstated explanation. 22.64 kg is carried because it is the datasheet's figure; what a Premium build is, and whether it changes anything on a face, is unknown. No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document either - the Available to Order block lists the PSU and fan SKUs only - so the configurations here carry no part-numbers.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ac","dc"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide or price list for the S9610 aggregation line","what":"chassis-variants"},{"note":"HIG section 8 says the grounding location 'is covered with a protective label' and step 5 says to remove it, but the rear product photograph shows a bare silver two-hole plate with no label on it. The plate is modelled as the photograph shows it. Whether the shipped unit has a label over it, and what colour, is not established here.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ground-mark","rear"],"wanted":"a photograph of an unopened unit's rear panel","what":"grounding-label"},{"note":"The HIG contradicts itself about installation depth in two places six pages apart. The Preparation Check List says the S9610-48DX 'need a minimum reserve depth of 36 inches (91.4cm)'; the Space Clearance paragraph works it out from the 762 mm chassis plus 6 inches of handle clearance front and back and concludes 'A total minimum reserve depth of 42 inches (106.6cm) is required'. Same measure, same scope, two values. Nothing in this model depends on it - the chassis depth itself is agreed at 762 mm by both documents - but a rack survey would.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["front","rear"],"wanted":"a revision of the HIG that reconciles its own two figures","what":"reserve-depth-disagreement"},{"note":"The datasheet calls the lower SFP quad '4 x 10G SFP+ management ports' and HIG Figure 4 labels it '4x SFP+ Management', and that is the whole of what is said about it. The HIG's Port Overview table - which gives form factor, reach and speed for 0-39, 40-47 and 48-51 - does not list these four at all, so there is no stated reach, no stated media list and no statement of what 'management' means here (out-of-band access, telemetry off-box, a second control plane). They are modelled as SFP+ openings numbered 0-3 with role management, which is what the two sources support and no more.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["sfp-plus-mgmt"],"wanted":"a port table or NOS guide covering the SFP+ management quad","what":"sfp-plus-management-role"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"3+1","redundancy-note":"3+1 - 3+1 hot-swappable (attrs fan-redundancy)"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster at the bottom left of the faceplate - the RS-232 console RJ45, the micro-USB serial console, the USB 3.0 maintenance port, the out-of-band RJ45 and the recessed reset button. Same block, and the same word for it, as the library's other UfiSpace white boxes","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"every indicator that belongs to a particular port - one lamp per QSFP28 port in the painted bands, one per QSFP-DD port on its blue strip, one per SFP28 port on the yellow band, and the two lamps in the out-of-band jack's own aperture","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 hot-swappable"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfpdd-400g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"400g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus-mgmt":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"description":"the 2x2 SFP+ quad below the SFP28 block, '4 x 10G SFP+ management ports' in the datasheet and '4x SFP+ Management' in HIG Figure 4's callout. Five media, one job, and the datasheet groups them under one heading, Timing Interfaces","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9610-48DX","name":"s9610-48dx","portfolio":{"family":"Open Aggregation Router","line":"Telecoms","series":"S9600 Series"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"attrs":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - Specifications, Environmental, Performance, Regulatory Compliance and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections; the GNSS receiver detail comes from the HIG's Installing an Antenna section. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied - note that this datasheet lists NEBS GR-63 and WEEE under Environment and NEBS GR-1089 under EMC, and they are filed where the vendor files them rather than gathered under one heading."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - '2 RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm or 17.17\" x 30\" x 3.45\"', 'Weight: 22.64kg or 49.91lb (without FRU)'; the HIG's Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple as 17.16\" x 30\" x 3.45\". 436 is the body and not a rack face: the HIG's Space Clearance paragraph states both numbers in one sentence - 'The S9610-48DX width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks' - so the ears are the 46.7 mm difference and are not drawn. The datasheet render corroborates it by drawing a short bracket tab OUTSIDE the full-height body on each side (px 0-8 and 1538 against a body of 10-1532). 87.7 mm is 1.98 rack units, which is why both documents call it 2RU. The 762 mm depth is the chassis without FRUs; the HIG adds that the fan handles project 29 mm and the PSU handles 30 mm, which is clearance rather than body. THE HIG GIVES TWO CHASSIS WEIGHTS, 'Standard: 49.91lb (22.64kg)' and 'Premium: 47.48lb (21.54kg)'; 22.64 is carried here because it is the one the datasheet publishes, and what separates the two builds is not stated anywhere - see the chassis-variants gap."},"connector-orientation":{"note":"photo/drawing. THE STACKED BITS/ToD PAIR IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: at 10x the upper jack's aperture has its latch keyway at the TOP with the contacts below, and the lower jack's keyway at the BOTTOM with the contacts along the top edge, so the two mirror and the upper is rotate: 180 against std/rj45-ganged, which draws pins up and keyway down. The console and out-of-band RJ45s at the bottom of the cluster are both keyway-down, unrotated. THE CAGE ROWS ARE NOT MEASURED AND ARE CARRIED FROM A SIBLING: neither the render nor the guide figure resolves a cage lip at this scale - a QSFP column at 10x shows a symmetric perforated EMI strip between its two openings and nothing that distinguishes them - so the belly-to-belly convention here (upper port rotate: 180, lower unrotated) is ufispace/s9600-56dx's reading of the same cage family, taken from that file and stated as borrowed rather than as a second measurement. See the cage-lip-orientation gap. The USB 3.0 socket IS measured: its opening is 4.8 wide by 12.9 tall, so it is portrait and std/usb-a is rotated 90."},"fans":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet 'FAN Types: FAN-808012-HCE, exhaust air flow', and the HIG's Component Physical Information table dimensions the part 81 x 154.8 x 81.5 mm - the same part number and the same three numbers ufispace/fan-808012 already carries from the S9321-64E guide, so the component is reused unchanged and this is a corroboration rather than a fork. Four bays, 3+1 redundant, hot-swappable."},"front-grid":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - the QSFP28 blocks sit on ONE four-row grid and it was taken from the port APERTURES, which the render draws EMPTY, not from any module face. Threshold-scanning a column through the first left-block column gives openings at 16.28-24.00, 31.42-39.42, 46.85-54.85 and 61.99-69.99 mm, i.e. row centres 20.14, 35.42, 50.85 and 65.99, and the same four rows come back within a tenth of a millimetre at all ten column centres. The least-squares grid is 20.14 + 15.283k, which is what is used: 20.14, 35.42, 50.71, 65.99. The one row that argues is row 2, whose ten readings average 50.80 against the grid's 50.71 - 0.09 mm, or a third of a pixel at this render's 3.5 px/mm, so it is absorbed rather than given its own number."},"grounding":{"note":"HIG section 8 - the router is grounded through a #6 AWG two-hole lug and M4 screws supplied in the kit, and the guide says 'The location for securing the grounding lug is at the rear of the case and is covered with a protective label' and later 'remove the protective label'. ONE location. The rear photograph shows that location as a bare silver two-hole plate with an earth symbol beside it and no label over it, so the plate is drawn as the photograph shows it and the label's absence is recorded in the grounding-label gap rather than invented onto the panel."},"legends":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing, positions and wording read off the datasheet render at 4-10x. Readable and drawn: 1PPS, 10MHZ, GNSS ANT, 'BITS (up) (down) TOD', SS for the USB 3.0 socket, RESET, the six system-lamp names, two IOIOI console marks, the network symbol under the out-of-band jack, the '0 (up) (down) 1 2 (up) (down) 3' legend under the SFP+ management quad, the forty QSFP28 numerals with their arrows, the eight QSFP-DD digits and the S9610-48DX wordmark at the bottom right. THE YELLOW BAND IS REAL PAINT and it is what ties the SFP28 quad to QSFP28 port 0: it runs from x 61.55 to 110.4 mm, which is the SFP block plus the left half of port 0's column, and the green band takes over at 110.5 - and the datasheet's only related sentence is that those four ports are 'In-band port share with 100GE Port 0'. The arrows on the yellow band sit about 2 mm to the right of their cage centres (marks centred on 71.15 and 85.41 against columns at 68.99 and 83.45); they are drawn where they are printed rather than snapped to the cages."},"lifecycle":{"note":"searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9610-48DX end of life' - no announcement found. The vendor's telco aggregation product page, the R1.9 hardware installation guide and the August 2024 launch announcement are all live, and distributors still list the part. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence."},"panel-metal":{"note":"THE BRIGHT SHELL AROUND EACH CAGE BLOCK IS PANEL, NOT PART. The datasheet render shows the real thing with every cage EMPTY: each QSFP28 column is one bright-bezelled 1x2 ganged block 19.8 mm wide with a perforated EMI strip between its two openings, and std/ parts draw the opening and stop. So each column is drawn here as one light decor rectangle 19.8 x 26.0 mm with its two apertures placed on it, and the same is done for the two QSFP-DD assemblies, the SFP28 quad and the SFP+ management quad. Without them the cages sit invisibly on a dark faceplate. The same reasoning puts a gold disc behind each coax jack (std/sma and std/smb draw the bore, not the knurled nut), a silver strip behind the stacked BITS/ToD pair, the two RJ45s at the bottom and the portrait USB 3.0 socket, and a white block under the six system-lamp legends, which the render prints dark on printed white."},"port-leds":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - ONE round lamp per port, and that is the whole rule on this panel, which is simpler than the S9600-56DX's mixture of four-lamp clusters and light-pipe strips. Each QSFP28 column carries two lamps in its band, 2.05 mm either side of the column centre and 2.5 mm across: forty lamps for forty ports, at y 12.50 in the upper band and 73.70 in the lower. Each QSFP-DD blue strip carries one lamp per row at y 36.03 and 50.47, eight for eight ports. The four SFP28 ports have four lamps on the yellow band at 68.42, 73.54, 82.70 and 87.85. WHICH lamp serves which port is taken from the adjacency of the printed numerals - the left lamp of a pair sits beside the even numeral and the right beside the odd - and not from any table; see the port-led-semantics gap. The out-of-band jack carries two lamps in its own aperture, drawn dark in the render."},"port-numbers":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing, and this device PRINTS its numbering on the metal, which the S9600-56DX does not. Each QSFP28 column carries, in the painted band outside it, an up arrow, the even port's numeral, two lamps, the odd port's numeral and a down arrow - '0 1' through '38 39' - and the numerals are legible at 4x in the datasheet render with the cages empty, so they are drawn here. THE QSFP-DD STRIPS PRINT A DIFFERENT NUMBERING FROM THE GUIDE'S: each blue strip carries a SINGLE DIGIT, 0 and 1 on the left strip of the first assembly, 2 and 3 on its right strip, 4/5 and 6/7 on the second assembly's, so the metal numbers the eight 400G ports 0-7 while HIG Figure 8's callout and the Port Overview table both number them 40-47. Both are recorded: the ids and rel-pos here are the guide's 40-47, because that is what a NOS and an operator will use, and the silkscreen draws the single digits because that is what is printed. The one legend that could NOT be read is the SFP28 block's - see the sfp28-band-numerals gap."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet 'Typical Power: 548 W (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG's Connecting Power sections state the maximum FOUR times, once per build and once per optics class: DC 1220 W under 400G optics MSA standards and 1524 W with OpenZR+ transceivers, AC 1212 W and 1510 W. Unlike the typical figure these ARE qualified, in a note printed beside them - 'Temperature: 45C, Optics: full populated, Traffic: 100% load'. 1524 is carried as power-max-w because max means the highest of the four, and the spread is recorded here rather than as a conflict: they are two builds and two optics classes, not four readings of one thing. Note that power-envelope therefore describes the TYPICAL figure's scope and not the maximum's, which is fully-configured with OpenZR+ and says so in this sentence. These are the vendor's figures as the vendor states them and are NOT reconciled against the module set: the fans publish no draw at all, so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor. PSU rating 2000 W per supply from the ordering lines; on a single 110 VAC feed the HIG derates each supply to 1000 W."},"psu-build":{"note":"the guide and the photograph agree here, unlike on the S9600-56DX. HIG Figures 5 and 17 draw an AC PSU and a DC PSU as the two orderable builds, and the rear product photograph shows the AC one: a vent grid on the left, a green lamp top-left, a dark pull strap and a three-slot IEC C20 inlet with a red release latch on the right, which is exactly what ufispace/psu-202-ac draws. NO LIBRARY LAMP FITS THAT: common/led-rect is the right shape and is 4.6 x 2.6, which is wider than the column and taller than the pitch, so six of them would overlap each other and lint would say so. common/led-dot is placed instead - the right pitch in the wrong shape, which is closer to the hardware than the right shape at the wrong pitch and is the only one of the two that does not collide. circle.data-description: S9321-64E HIG Fan FRU LED table - Off (BMC is not up), Green (Fan FRU function normal), Amber (Fan FRU is abnormal, the fan speed is under 4500rpm)

circle.data-states: off ok critical standby input-lost warning
circle.data-description: HIG PSU FRU LED table - Off (no input power to all power supplies), Green (output ON and OK), Red (a critical event causing a shutdown - failure, overcurrent, short circuit, over voltage, fan failure or over temperature), Blinking Green (standby state, input power present and only +5VSB on; the firmware-updating boot-loader row is visually identical and shares this state), Blinking Red (input cord unplugged or input lost with a second supply in parallel still fed), Blinking between Green and Red (warning events where the supply keeps operating - high temp, high power, high current, slow fan)

circle.data-states: off ok critical standby input-lost warning
circle.data-description: HIG PSU FRU LED table - Off (no input power to all power supplies), Green (output ON and OK), Red (a critical event causing a shutdown - failure, overcurrent, short circuit, over voltage, fan failure or over temperature), Blinking Green (standby state, input power present and only +5VSB on; the firmware-updating boot-loader row is visually identical and shares this state), Blinking Red (input cord unplugged or input lost with a second supply in parallel still fed), Blinking between Green and Red (warning events where the supply keeps operating - high temp, high power, high current, slow fan)
